FOLLOWUP 1 -- PUT THE MEASURED EFFECT IN THE CHRONICLE.

book/src/chronicle/the-murrain.md describes the MODEL -- the statistical substrate, metapopulations, persistence, the two linked population truths. It does not say what the model DID. Your headline trailer is "disease becomes a population-scale world phenomenon"; the chronicle should carry the population-scale measurement that earns it. Everything below is already measured and lives in your ledger or on this board; none of it needs re-deriving.

  SEED 42, from the committed fixtures (main vs your merge):
    occupation records   1,212 -> 1,061
    ended                  822 ->   754
    alive                  390 ->   307
    historical columns     452 ->   377
    present columns        389 ->   307
    distinct peoples        15 ->    15   (none extinct)

  THE SHAPE IS REDISTRIBUTION, NOT ATTRITION. Seven peoples lose ~210 living
  occupations, seven gain ~127; the net -83 is the residue of ~340 changing
  hands:
    kobold 130->22  wood-elf 29->2  desert-dwarf 34->11  hill-dwarf 26->6
    drow 24->5  desert-elf 13->3  gnoll 5->2
    bugbear 63->102  human 7->40  hobgoblin 40->59  gully-dwarf 3->19
    goblin 6->15  high-elf 2->11  snow-elf 5->7  sea-elf 3->3

  ACROSS 1,000 WORLDS (committed census, main vs yours):
    settlement-count   264.7 -> 259.9  (-1.8%)
    total-population  7383.8 -> 7219.3 (-2.2%)
    kobold settlements  41.0 ->  38.1  (-7.1%)
    peoples-placed     14.905 -> 14.914 (unchanged)

  AND THE MEAN HIDES THE EFFECT, which is the sentence worth writing:
    total-population  median -0.74%  p5 -41.1%  p95 +68.2%  worst -66.1%
    settlement-count  median -1.44%  p5 -43.0%  p95 +77.7%  worst -67.7%
  Worlds lose two thirds or gain two thirds; the aggregate is flat because the
  swings cancel. A 2% mean is not "the plague did almost nothing" -- it is a
  redistribution's mean by construction.

  (Caveat to carry: kobold's +1300% p95 is small denominators, 1 -> 14. Trust
  the loss tail, not the gain tail, or state it in absolute counts.)

  Two more results already in your record and not in the book: founder

FOLLOWUP 2 -- RESTORE THE EXPOSURE DISTINCTNESS GUARD, FAMILY-AWARE.

cfa5d64a614b removed the "two peoples root X under the same roman" assertion
from FOUR concepts -- hill, marsh, spring, valley -- when only marsh was
failing. The homophony argument was right: goblin and hobgoblin are kin and
both root 'marsh' as "Kotoa", which is a lexicon deriving from a shared
proto-language working correctly. The deletion was broader than that argument
supports, and it leaves two UNRELATED peoples colliding undetectable across all
four concepts -- which is a real naming defect and is what the guard was for.

The kin relation is reachable from the test:

  windows/worldgen/src/lib.rs:6924
    pub fn family_daughter_kinds(wc: &WorldComponents, family: &str) -> Vec<KindId>

Shape: group `rooted` by language family; assert distinct romans ACROSS
families; permit -- or better, ASSERT -- homophony WITHIN a family. That last
inversion is the stronger test: "goblin and hobgoblin share 'Kotoa' because
they are kin" is a positive claim about the language model, and a test that
states it beats one that merely tolerates it.

Do not restore a blanket distinctness check; it would red on the legitimate
kin case again.

NEITHER IS URGENT AND BOTH ARE SMALL. If you would rather they became registry
rows for a later campaign than a branch tonight, say so and I will record that
instead -- but say which, so they do not evaporate.
